title: NIST World Trade Center Reports (NCSTAR 1 & 1A)
summary: Federal Building and Fire Safety Investigation of the World Trade Center Disaster. Concludes each tower collapsed from aircraft impact damage, dislodged fireproofing and multi-floor fires — floor trusses sagged, pulled exterior columns inward, progressive collapse. WTC 7 (NCSTAR 1A, Nov 2008): thermal expansion failed Column 79 — 'the first known instance of the total collapse of a tall building primarily due to fires.' NIST's FAQ directly rebuts controlled demolition/thermite: no blast evidence; a thermite operation would have needed many thousands of pounds placed inconspicuously.
tldr: NIST NCSTAR 1 (December 2005) is the federal investigation of how aircraft impacts and subsequent fires collapsed the Twin Towers — built on 42 companion reports, nearly 1,200 first-person interviews, and computer simulations, ending with 30 building-safety recommendations.
ai_summary:
AI review of the NIST publication page for the towers investigation final report, read in full:
- Scope: the report 'describes how the aircraft impacts and subsequent fires led to the collapse of the towers,' plus evacuation/emergency-response evaluation, design and construction practices review, and code revisions; it was conducted under the National Construction Safety Team Act.
- Method: in-house expertise plus private-sector technical experts, accumulated documents/photos/videos, computer simulations of each tower on September 11, 2001, and nearly 1,200 first-person interviews of occupants and emergency responders.
- Published December 1, 2005 with 42 companion reports, ending in 30 recommendations on structural integrity, fire endurance, active fire protection, evacuation, and emergency response.
- DISCREPANCY: the record summary's claims about WTC 7 (NCSTAR 1A) and the FAQ's controlled-demolition/thermite rebuttal are not covered by this source — the page states the WTC 7 report 'will appear in a separate report.' The towers-report portion of the summary is broadly consistent.
